source.title: Theory of Deep Learning III: explaining the non-overfitting puzzle
source.authors: T. Poggio; Kenji Kawaguchi; Q. Liao; B. Miranda; L. Rosasco; X. Boix; J. Hidary; H. Mhaskar

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some OCR or transcription glitches appear, but the relevant experiments and captions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Reports CIFAR training classification-error behavior for networks trained with gradient methods, including random-label fitting and a setting where overfitting appears; these results bear on V1 using experiments related to, but not identical to, the version's recipes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's directly described CIFAR classification-error results. The paper's general propositions and cited findings are not rows. Figure 5's cross-entropy loss and other results about test loss do not measure a version's training-error claim.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR convolutional-network training classification errors, including zero error with scrambled labels and recovery to zero after perturbations. These bear on V1 using GD and related training recipes. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that gradient dynamics near suitable global minima resemble degenerate linear systems, providing a qualitative explanation for loss overfitting without classification-error overfitting on suitable datasets. This is conditional on assumptions about the minima and data, rather than a universal claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient descent and SGD in CIFAR experiments, with cross-entropy or square loss, and tests perturbation recovery and model-size effects; it does not reproduce the combined CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 SGD-or-Adam random-initialization recipes in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Model activation and size, label condition, training objective, and perturbation condition vary across the reported CIFAR results.
record.problems: Several relevant CIFAR findings are conveyed only in figures without stated training classification-error values; random initialization is not specified for the relevant CIFAR experiments, and the width-sweep caption's explicit zero-error result applies to polynomial networks.
record.rows_left_out: No row for Figure 5's cross-entropy loss over model size because it measures loss rather than classification error. Figure 1's random-label CIFAR result is retained as figure-only (R2), without inferring plotted values.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, partially corrupted labels, Adam, and verified random initialization are not reported for these results. Readable results do not establish the smaller-model, early-stopping or regularized-recipe qualifications. Exact training errors across the SGD width sweep are unavailable.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, recovery and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization. Retaining batch normalization supplies no such comparison.

missing.what: Figure 9 compares training and testing error for corresponding polynomial and ReLU convolutional networks; Section 6.4.2 reports very similar performance. Add the training-error comparison, marking absolute values unreadable from the supplied text.

Figure 10 supplies additional normal-label and scrambled-label CIFAR training-error results for the polynomial convolutional network. These conditions are absent from the rows; their plotted values cannot be recovered from this text.

Figure 17 presents the CIFAR polynomial-network square-loss experiment for comparison with Figure 6. Record its training classification-error results if the plot becomes available; no numerical verdict is possible from the supplied caption.

record.verdict_notes: The explicit zero-error statement in Section 2 resolves R2 without reading its plot. Unreadable figures and unspecified recipe details do not justify limits_scope or challenges labels. The local Hessian theory assumes zero-error minima and does not independently establish that training reaches them.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare SGD with Adam, sweep smaller models or early stopping as V1 describes, or report CIFAR-100; its CIFAR-10 results include a small ReLU network, a width sweep with SGD, and a polynomial-network figure.

rows.subject: 5-layer all convolutional network with ReLUs
rows.size_stated: 16 channels per hidden layer; W ≈ 10000 weights
rows.operation_detail: Trained with GD on cross-entropy; after reaching zero training classification error, repeatedly perturbed weights and continued GD until the training error returned to zero.

conditions.value: Gaussian noise; standard deviation 14 of that of the weights of the corresponding layer; added after every 100 training epochs

rows.baseline: 0 after roughly 1800 epochs of GD, before perturbations
rows.value: Training error reset to zero after added perturbations
rows.note: Caption describes the reset to zero after each perturbation; no numeric post-perturbation values are given.
rows.check: The architecture and size were copied from Figure 1 incorrectly. Figure 3 specifies four convolutional layers with 16, 32, 64 and 128 channels, followed by a fully connected layer; approximately 10,000 weights is not stated for this network. Zero training classification error occurs before perturbation and returns afterward. The noise scale rendered as '14' appears to be a lost fraction; its intended value cannot be verified from the supplied text. Batch normalization is retained in the CIFAR experiments.

rows.subject: 5-layer all convolutional network with ReLUs
rows.size_stated: 16 channels per hidden layer; W ≈ 10000 weights
rows.operation_detail: Trained on subsets of CIFAR; labels randomly scrambled.
rows.note: The caption identifies random-label training, but the text does not state its training classification-error values; the plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: The value is not exclusively figure-only: Section 2 explicitly states that the network in Figure 1 achieves zero training error on randomly labeled data. Replace the unreadable value with that textual result, without assigning it to every subset size. Batch normalization is retained.

rows.subject: 5-layer all convolutional convolutional network with ReLUs
rows.size_stated: all hidden layers have same number of channels; model parameters swept, exact sizes not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size while training on a fixed CIFAR-10 training set using SGD.
rows.note: The text says classification error does not change across the parameter sweep, but does not state the training error values. Figure 5's explicit overfitting statement concerns cross-entropy loss, not training classification error.
rows.check: The supplied text does not preserve readable training-error values from Figure 6. The discussion of unchanged classification error and lack of test overfitting does not establish zero training error at particular widths. Batch normalization is retained.

rows.subject: 5-layer all convolutional polynomial network
rows.size_stated: all hidden layers have same number of channels; exact sizes not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied model size on a fixed CIFAR training set; all ReLU activations replaced by degree-10 polynomial approximations.

conditions.value: normal, as opposed to the separately described randomly scrambled-label setup

rows.note: Caption explicitly states zero error for W ≥ n; this is a polynomial network, not the corresponding ReLU network.
rows.check: Figure 11 explicitly reports zero error for W ≥ n. Polynomial activations remain within V1's convolutional-network scope, although the exact optimizer and initialization for this figure are not specified. Batch normalization is retained.

rows.subject: deep polynomial network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR with GD optimizing the square-loss risk.
rows.note: Caption states that overfitting appears for classification error, but the figure-only training classification-error value is not described in text.
rows.check: Figure 18 reports classification-error overfitting but supplies no readable training-error value in this text. Overfitting alone establishes neither zero nor substantial training error. The network's detailed architecture is not independently specified in this caption.
